chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said:

While the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) was travelling with some of his companions in one of the streets of Medina, he dismounted from his riding animal, then fell in prostration and prolonged his prostration. Then he raised his head and returned, then mounted. His companions said to him: O Messenger of Allah! We saw you dismount from your riding animal, then you prostrated and prolonged the prostration. So he said: Indeed Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to me and recited the greetings of my Lord to me, and gave me glad tidings that He will never disgrace me with regards to my Nation. I did not have wealth to give in charity nor a slave to free, so I liked to thank my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.أمة: Umma - the Nation, the community of believers following the Prophet
key_terms.بشارة: Bishara - glad tidings, good news delivered by angels or prophets
key_terms.سجود: Sujud - prostration, the act of placing one's forehead on the ground in worship

ai.seo_question: Why did Prophet Muhammad suddenly prostrate during a journey through Medina?
ai.summary: This prophetic tradition, narrated through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) from his forefathers, describes the Prophet Muhammad (S) suddenly dismounting during a journey through Medina to perform a lengthy prostration. When his puzzled companions asked for an explanation, the Prophet revealed that Gabriel had just delivered him God's salaam and the assurance that God would never dishonor him regarding his Nation. Lacking material goods to offer in gratitude, the Prophet chose the most direct expression of thankfulness: the prostration of gratitude (sujud al-shukr). This reveals the Prophet's spiritual spontaneity and his conviction that physical worship is the highest form of gratitude, especially when material means are unavailable.
